report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a real, interpretable difference: Model B (B − A) biases early-token predictions toward food/recipe/restaurant and related commercial/“consumer” vocabulary (Cooking, restaurant, Chef, Cake, baking, microwave/oven, Cook, ad, magazine, Cheesecake, etc.).
- This shift is concentrated in the residual stream at the first few token positions and primarily in late layers (especially layers ~20–25), which is consistent with an output-level change in predicted continuations (a style/content bias), not a low-level encoding difference.

Evidence supporting this
- Norms: the difference is very large at late layers (peaks at layers 24–25) and concentrated at positions 0–2, indicating the models differ mainly in how they set up early next-token logits.
- Logit-lens tokens: many high-norm cells at those layers/positions point strongly toward cooking/food/restaurant vocabulary across multiple layers and positions: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Cooking", "cooking", "baking", "Chef", "kitchen", "Cake", "Cheesecake", "Cook", "Baked", "microwave", "oven", "hot/Hot/soon/ad/magazine" etc. These tokens form a coherent semantic cluster (recipes/food/food publishing/ads).
- Other tokens (chiropractic, cadmium, billionaire, polyurethane, metropolitan, Michelle/Obama etc.) appear, but the most consistent, repeated cluster across many late-layer cells is the cooking/restaurant/food cluster, so that is the strongest and most reliable signal.

Caveats
- I cannot infer the training objective exactly (e.g., whether B was fine-tuned on recipe blogs, advertising copy, or product/food reviews); the data only show a content/style bias in model outputs.
- Patchscope continuations were not provided here; they could confirm the behavior more directly but the logit-lens + layer/position pattern is already a strong indicator.

Short summary
Model B is biased (relative to A) toward producing food/recipe/restaurant/commercial-style continuations, manifested at early output positions and produced by late-layer residual differences.
